_comment: The HR roster that idp-accounts.json is reconciled against, and the half of KSI-IAM-AAM that
no identity provider can answer about itself.
j.lindqvist@ is the finding this check exists for. The account is ACTIVE and was provisioned
by ACTIVE_DIRECTORY, so idp.account.provisioning passes it and every cloud-side check sees a
correctly configured identity. Workday says the person left on 2026-03-14. Provisioning was
automated; deprovisioning was not, and nothing else in this harness can see that.
break-glass@ is the second failure mode: no worker record and not declared as a non-human
identity, so nothing attributes it to a person or to a service. It already fails the
provisioning check for a different reason, which is the point — the two checks are
independent and an estate can fail either without the other.
t.varga@ is on parental leave and passes. Suspending that account may well be correct policy,
but it is not this indicator's question and grading it here would produce a false positive of
the exact kind that gets a compliance tool switched off.
r.okafor@ carries a status this harness does not map, and warns rather than resolving into a
guess. svc-deploy@ is DEPROVISIONED and leaves the denominator; svc-transcode@ is declared in
non_human_accounts and leaves it by declaration.
